old_title: Is Slovenia v Scotland on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations League
new_title: Scotland miss chances in goalless draw with Slovenia to begin Pocognoli era

Scotland kick off a new era under Sebastien Pocognoli as the Tartan Army face Slovenia in the Nations League.
The 39-year-old former Belgium international Pocognoli was a left-field replacement for Steve Clarke, who resigned following Scotland's group-stage exit form the World Cup.
Pocognoli has selected a new-look squad for the Nations League games against Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia, with Scotland returning to League B of the competition.
He has promised a more energetic, front-foot style of play as Scotland look to the future and build up to Euro 2028, when they will be co-hosts. Here's everything you need to know
When is Slovenia v Scotland?
Kick-off in Ljubljana is at 2pm BST on Saturday 26 September.
How can I watch it?
It will be shown on BBC One, with coverage from 1:45pm.
What is the team news?
In terms of absences, Pocognoli is without Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland, while Kieran Tierney and Kenny McLean also withdrew from the squad.
Hull City striker Oli McBurnie has been recalled to the Scotland squad and could make his first appearance since 2021, while Swansea defender Stephen Welsh, Celtic right-back Colby Donovan, Brondby defender Luis Binks, Stoke centre-back Luke Graham, Hearts winger Josh McPake and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure have all received their first call-ups.
McBurnie and Ure could feature in the attack, due to absences of Adams, Shankland and Steve Clarke favourite Lyndon Dykes, while Welsh and Binks could come straight into a new-look defence, potentially as part of a back-three.
Slovenia, meanwhile, will be without Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko, who is still dealing with a shin issue.
Possible Scotland line-up
Gunn; Welsh, Binks, McKenna; Hickey, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McGinn; Ure, McBurnie

Scotland football's ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sebastien Pocognoli's tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.
The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke's successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.
Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, with Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie both squandering good chances.
However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager's debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.
Follow all the action from Pocognoli's first game with our live blog below:
McBurnie admits 'I should have scored'
Oli McBurnie chats to the BBC after that draw and acknowledged that he should have scored with one of his chances.
McBurnie said: "It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.
"We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.
"I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I'd rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.
"Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two."
Sebastien Pocognoli begins with a draw
Sebastien Pocognoli is going to be a pretty animated figure on the sidelines it seems. He gets a point in his first game as Scotland boss
FULL-TIME Slovenia 0-0 Scotland
And it's all over. It ends 0-0, so Sebastien Pocognoli's first game sees him take a point away from home but Scotland probably should have won it in the second half. Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie both missed golden chances.
On the flip side, they were rubbish in the first half and didn't truly test Jan Oblak enough, so perhaps a draw wasn't the end of the world overall
Slovenia 0-0 Scotland, 90+2 mins
Sturm thinks he should have a corner as Welsh blocks his cross but the ball was determined to have already crossed the line before he hooked it across, so it's a goal-kick.
Scotland then try to mount one final attack but Hendry's ball into the box is straight at Oblak. This is going to end 0-0
Slovenia 0-0 Scotland, 90 mins
Just two minutes of added time. Hmmm...
Slovenia won't mind that, while Scotland probably would've preferred a little longer to grab a winner. Can they fashion one last chance?
Slovenia 0-0 Scotland, 89 mins
The pitch is an absolute mess now, by the way. Just covered in divots where it has cut up. McGinn lofts a free-kick into the box but Oblak is off his line well to claim confidently.
We're lurching towards injury time here.
Slovenia 0-0 Scotland, 87 mins
Gannon-Doak links up well with McGinn, cuts back on to his left foot and lifts a cross to the back post but it doesn't quite fall for Scotland.
Can they find a way to force a dramatic late winner?
WATCH: Scotland miss key chances
One of these had to go in didn't they? McBurnie and Bowie both miss good chances in the second half
Slovenia 0-0 Scotland, 82 mins
Slovenia haven't got out of their half for about 30 minutes it feels like. Robertson whips in another cross, Oblak tries to punch clear but the connection isn't great. However, Slovenia scramble clear.
Scotland would be good value for a winner if they can find one. It's now 15 shots to 3 in this match in favour of the Scots...
